body:
Rafael Mendes: Heads up #eng — we’re starting a *beta* rollout of the new Incident Bot “context bundles” (deploy + config diff + saturation snapshot). Goal is to make the first 2–3 min of triage less painful + reduce the “what changed?” ping-pong.

What you’ll see (in #incidents threads):
• Recent deploys / rollouts per service + region (with PR + pipeline links)
• Config diffs (routing policy + flags) with redaction
• Saturation snapshot (queue depth / throttling / GPU pressure) + links to canonical dashboards

This is *beta*: expect some missing data / noisy edges. It should fail open (post partial bundle w/ clear errors).

How to report issues / feedback:
• Reply in-thread with a screenshot/link + what you expected
• Or file a bug in the incident-bot repo (tag @Jacob Stein) and link the incident thread
• Noise / paging concerns: tag @Aisha Bello

Enablement is gated by feature flag (per-channel) so we can ramp without spamming everyone.

Feature flag enablement snippet (channel scoped):
```bash
# enable collectors beta in a channel
rbctl flags set incident-bot.collectors-beta true \
  --scope channel:#incidents \
  --ttl 14d \
  --reason "beta rollout - incident context bundles"

# optional: enable restricted-mode posting (sensitive incidents)
rbctl flags set incident-bot.restricted-mode true \
  --scope channel:#incidents \
  --reason "post full bundle to restricted channel"
```
If you want your team channel added to the allowlist, drop the channel name here + who’s on-call owning it.

Sean Gallagher: +1 — please be brutal about formatting/readability. If it’s not usable in the first scroll, it’s a fail. We’re iterating fast.

Jacob Stein: For folks curious: bundles are collector-based (deploy/config/sat). Each collector has a hard timeout + caching keyed to (incident, time window), so it shouldn’t hammer metrics/logs during a big event.

Chloe Martin: Does this post automatically on incident creation or only after someone runs a command?

Rafael Mendes: Automatic on incident creation + when severity flips to SEV0/SEV1. (We may dial this back if it’s too chatty.) There’s also `/incbot context` to re-run if the window has moved.

Aisha Bello: If it feels spammy: tell us *which section* is noisy (deploy list vs config diff vs sat). We can tighten time windows or collapse blocks. Also watching bot post rate + thread clutter.

Logan Wright: FYI saturation collector uses the new normalized labels. If you see “unknown region” or missing model labels, link it — that likely means the pipeline is dropping tags.

Priya Natarajan: On config diffs: reminder that we’re only posting allowlisted keys in beta. If you notice something important missing, tell us the key name + why you need it, and we’ll evaluate if it’s safe to add.

Marcus Lin: +1 and please treat anything that looks like customer identifiers as a bug. If you see payload-ish fields in a bundle, DM me + @Jacob Stein, and we’ll lock it down.

Devon Price: For enablement, does `rbctl` require being in eng-sre? Some folks won’t have permissions.

Rafael Mendes: Yep, currently limited. If you want this in your channel, just reply here and we’ll flip it / add the allowlist entry. We’ll also put a self-serve request flow in place once we’re confident about noise.

Connor O'Brien: Deploy section should include canary % when available. If you see a deploy entry without rollout phase/canary status, ping me — might be a missing field from release events.

deploy-bot: deploy event: inference-router @ us-east-1 — rollout started (canary 10%) — build `router-2025.02.09.3` — https://github.com/redwood/redwood/actions/runs/812233991

Sean Gallagher: ^ this is exactly the type of thing we want the bundle to surface when an incident starts. If you see a canary deploy but the bundle doesn’t call it out, that’s a bug.

Chloe Martin: Where does the bot post the restricted-mode “full bundle”? Want to make sure folks know where to look.

Jacob Stein: Currently `#incidents-restricted` (membership is on-call + SRE + security). The public thread gets a minimal stub with links + “restricted mode enabled” note.

Aisha Bello: Also: if you *disable* the bot in a thread because it’s getting in the way, please say why. “Too long” is actionable, “annoying” is… less so :)

Logan Wright: One more: if you see saturation numbers that look stale (e.g. 15m old during active burn), screenshot the timestamp line in the bundle. We added fallback behavior when metrics lag, but we might need better wording.

Rafael Mendes: Thanks all. We’ll post weekly updates w/ fixes + rollout changes. Keep the feedback coming, especially from folks actively on-call this week.
